title: Past continuous and pluperfect
intro: A story needs more than one kind of past. You know the plain past `-dY` ([A2 unit 1](a2-u01)), which tells what happened. This unit adds two more: the past continuous `-ýArdY`, for what was going on (*Ýagyş ýagýardy*, it was raining), and the pluperfect `-(Y)pdY`, for what had already happened (*Film eýýäm başlanypdy*, the film had already started). Both are built the same way, from a form you know plus the past `-dY`, and the third section sets out that pattern, which the next unit uses three more times. Last come the small words that move a story along: *birden*, *şol wagt*, *şondan soň*, *eýýäm* and *entek*.

blocks.text: Take the present `-ýAr` ([A1 unit 6](a1-u06)), add `-dY`, then the endings of the past: *-m, -ň, —, -k, -ňYz, -lAr*. *gelýär* (comes) → *gelýärdim*, I was coming; *okaýar* (reads) → *okaýardym*, I was reading. The vowel of `-dY` follows the vowel just before it: *-di* after *-ýär*, *-dy* after *-ýar*.

Everything you know about `-ýAr` stays the same: *t* softens in the verbs that soften (*gidýärdim*, *edýärdim*), and a final *e* stays *e* before it (*işleýärdim*). Because `-ýArdY` has an ending in every person, the pronoun can be left out: *Okaýardym*, I was reading.

**What it's for.** `-ýArdY` describes a past situation from the inside, while it was going on. Use it for the background of a story, the scene in which something happens: *Men öýe gelenimde, ýagyş ýagýardy*, when I came home, it was raining. Use it for an action that something else interrupted: *Men kitap okaýardym, birden yşyk öçdi*, I was reading a book, and suddenly the light went out. And use it for what went on over a stretch of the past: *Şol wagt Aýna Aşgabatda ýaşaýardy*, at that time Aýna was living in Ashgabat.

items.en: When I came home, it was raining.

items.tk: Men kitap okaýardym, birden yşyk öçdi.
items.seg: Men kitap oka|ýar|dy|m, birden yşyk öç|di.
items.en: I was reading a book, and suddenly the light went out.
We were drinking tea.
The children were sleeping.
At that time Aýna was living in Ashgabat.

blocks.text: **Wasn't doing.** The negative is the negative of `-ýAr`, *-mA* before it, then `-dY` and the ending: *gelmeýärdim*, I wasn't coming; *okamaýardym*, I wasn't reading.

**Was … doing?** The question particle comes **before** `-dY`, right after `-ýAr`, just as it comes before `-dY` with nouns (*talypmydyň?*, [A2 unit 2](a2-u02)): *Sen uklaýarmydyň?* Were you sleeping? *Ýagyş ýagýarmydy?* Was it raining? With a question word there is no particle: *Sen näme edýärdiň?* What were you doing?

**Sitting, standing, lying: the helpers in the past.** In [A2 unit 11](a2-u11) you met `-(Y)p` with *otyr, dur, ýatyr, ýör* for what is going on now: *Ol kitap okap otyr*. Put the helper in the past with `-dY` and the endings, and you have another past continuous, which also shows the posture: *Men kitap okap otyrdym*, I was (sitting) reading a book.

blocks.caption: The helpers with `-dY`
head: Turkmen
Meaning
rows: We were (standing) waiting for the bus.
He was working in Mary (for a while).

blocks.text: Only the helper changes: *otyrdym, otyrdyň, otyrdy…* After *dur* and *ýör* the vowel rounds in the second syllable: *durdum*, *ýördüm*. As in the present, `-ýArdY` is always right too: *Men kitap okaýardym*.

blocks.title: Plain past or -ýArdY?
blocks.text: *Ýagyş ýagdy* reports an event: it rained. *Ýagyş ýagýardy* paints the scene: it was raining (when something else happened). In a story, `-ýArdY` sets things up and `-dY` moves them on: *Ýagyş ýagýardy. Birden Merdan geldi.*

blocks.title: Where the particle goes
blocks.text: The particle goes before `-dY`: *uklaýarmydyň?*, not `uklaýardyňmy`. And don't drop the *ýa* of a vowel stem: *oka-ýar-dym*, *işle-ýär-dim*.

To say what **had** happened before another moment in the past, take `-(Y)p` ([A2 unit 5](a2-u05)), add `-dY` and the past endings: *gelip* → *gelipdim*, I had come; *okap* → *okapdym*, I had read. *Men wokzala baranymda, otly eýýäm gidipdi*: when I got to the station, the train had already left. The train left first; `-(Y)pdY` looks back at it from the moment you arrived.

The rules of `-(Y)p` apply as you know them: *-yp, -ip* after a consonant and *-p* after a vowel; the vowel rounds in the second syllable (*görüpdim*, *bolupdym*); a final *e* becomes *ä* (*işläpdim*); and the *t*-verbs soften (*gidipdim*, *edipdim*, *aýdypdym*). Then `-dY` follows the vowel of `-(Y)p`: *gelipdim* but *okapdym*.

items.tk: Men wokzala baranymda, otly eýýäm gidipdi.
items.seg: Men wokzal|a bar|an|ym|da, otly eýýäm gid|ip|di.
items.en: When I got to the station, the train had already left.

items.tk: Men kinoteatra gelenimde, film eýýäm başlanypdy.
items.seg: Men kinoteatr|a gel|en|im|de, film eýýäm başlan|yp|dy.
items.en: When I got to the cinema, the film had already started.
I had seen him before.
The cat had run away.
I had lost my key.

blocks.text: **Hadn't done.** The negative of `-(Y)p` is `-mAn`, with *ä* for front vowels: *gelmän*, *okaman* (you will meet it on its own in [B1 unit 7](b1-u07)). Add `-dY` and the endings: *gelmändim*, I hadn't come; *okamandym*, I hadn't read.
**Had … done?** Once more the particle comes before `-dY`: *gelipmidiň?*, had you come? *Film başlanypmydy?* Had the film started?

blocks.title: Already and not yet
blocks.text: `-(Y)pdY` goes well with *eýýäm* and *entek*: *Ol eýýäm gidipdi*, she had already left; *Ol entek gelmändi*, he hadn't come yet. With *entek*, the verb is negative.

blocks.title: -(Y)pdY or -(Y)pdYr?
blocks.text: One letter apart, two different things. *Ol gelipdi*: he had come (before some moment in the past). *Ol gelipdir*: he has come, as you can see or as you've heard ([A2 unit 2](a2-u02)). [B1 unit 3](b1-u03) is about the second.

`-ýArdY` and `-(Y)pdY` are built the same way, and so are the pasts of the next unit. Take a verb form, add `-dY`, then the endings of the past. It is the same `-dY` you put on nouns to say **was** ([A2 unit 2](a2-u02)): *talyp-dy-m*, I was a student; *gelýär-di-m*, I was coming.

Three rules hold for all of them. **The negative stays inside the first part**: *gel-me-ýär-di-m*, *gel-män-di-m*. **The particle comes before `-dY`**: *gelýär-mi-di-m?*, *gelip-mi-di-m?* **The endings are always those of the past**, *-m, -ň, —, -k, -ňYz, -lAr*, never the endings of the present: *gelýärdim*, not `gelýärdirin`.

items.en: I wasn't listening to you.
Were you sleeping?
We hadn't seen this film.
Had you seen this film before?

blocks.title: The vowel of -dY
blocks.text: `-dY` takes its vowel from the syllable just before it: *gelýär-di*, *okaýar-dy*, *gelip-di*, *okap-dy*, *otyr-dy*. Only *dur* and *ýör*, one-syllable helpers with a rounded vowel, round it: *durdy* but *durdum*, *ýördi* but *ýördüm*.

sections.title: Telling a story: birden, şol wagt, şondan soň

blocks.text: A few small words carry a story forward. You know *ilki*, *soňra*, *ondan soň* and *iň soňunda* from [A2 unit 11](a2-u11), and *eýýäm* and *entek* from [A2 unit 1](a2-u01). Add these:

items: *birden*: suddenly. Something happens at a moment, so the verb is in the plain past: *Birden yşyk öçdi*.
*şol wagt*: at that moment, just then; also **at that time**, for a longer stretch: *Şol wagt Merdan geldi*; *Şol wagt men talypdym*.
*şondan soň*: after that. It means the same as *ondan soň* and points back to what you've just told: *Şondan soň biz bile çaý içdik*.
*eýýäm*: already; *entek*, with a negative: not yet. Both often go with `-(Y)pdY`: *Ol eýýäm gidipdi*; *Ol entek gelmändi*.

blocks.text: **Three pasts in one story.** A story usually sets its scene with `-ýArdY`, moves forward with `-dY` and looks back with `-(Y)pdY`. Here is a short one; notice which verb does which job.

items.tk: Düýn agşam men öýde kitap okaýardym.
items.seg: Düýn agşam men öý|de kitap oka|ýar|dy|m.
items.en: Last night I was at home reading a book.
It was raining outside.
Suddenly the light went out.
At that moment someone knocked at the door.

items.tk: Gapyny açdym: Merdan eken! Onuň hem yşygy öçüpdi.
items.seg: Gapy|ny aç|dy|m: Merdan eken! On|uň hem yşyg|y öç|üp|di.
items.en: I opened the door: it was Merdan! His light had gone out too.

items.tk: Şondan soň biz bile çaý içdik.
items.seg: Şondan soň biz bile çaý iç|di|k.
items.en: After that we had tea together.

lines.tk: Düýn näme boldy? Sen näme üçin gijä galdyň?
lines.en: What happened yesterday? Why were you late?
I was waiting for the bus at the stop.

lines.tk: Birden bir çaga ýykyldy. Men oňa kömek etdim.
lines.en: Suddenly a child fell over. I helped him.

lines.tk: Şondan soň duralga seretdim: awtobus eýýäm gidipdi!
lines.en: After that I looked at the stop: the bus had already gone!

blocks.title: birden takes the plain past
blocks.text: What happens suddenly is an event, so after *birden* the verb is in `-dY`: *Birden yşyk öçdi*, not `öçýärdi`. The scene around it can be in `-ýArdY`: *Men okaýardym, birden yşyk öçdi*.

summary: **Was doing**: `-ýAr` + `-dY` + *-m, -ň, —, -k, -ňYz, -lAr*: *gelýärdim*, *okaýardym*. It sets the scene or tells what was interrupted.
Negative *gelmeýärdim*; question with the particle before `-dY`: *gelýärmidiň?*
With a helper: *okap otyrdym*, *garaşyp durduk*, *uklap ýatyrdy*, *işläp ýördüm*.
**Had done**: `-(Y)p` + `-dY` + the past endings: *gelipdim*, *okapdym*; negative *gelmändim*; question *gelipmidiň?*
Every compound past is a verb form + `-dY` + the past endings; the negative stays inside, the particle comes before `-dY`.
Stories: `-ýArdY` for the scene, `-dY` for events, `-(Y)pdY` to look back; *birden*, *şol wagt*, *şondan soň*, *eýýäm*, *entek*.
